isolation.note: Verified against OpenCode 1.18.31 (verified live during development): OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT is honored as an inline config override; tools.{"*": false} disables every tool, permission.{"*": "deny"} denies execution, plugin [] and --pure drop plugins, mcp {} drops MCP servers, and a live probe confirmed the model can emit no executing tool calls. Residual limitation: OpenCode merges user-global config (~/.config/opencode) and managed settings that this harness cannot un-merge, so globally declared plugins/MCP servers may still be loaded (their execution remains denied). Claim: denied tool EXECUTION in a fresh session and fresh temp cwd; NOT a hermetic sandbox.

proposal.rationale: Weight-stationary dataflow. For each n-block (outer), k-blocks accumulate in order into two 16-row accumulator blocks (m0 at acc rows 0-15, m1 at rows 16-31), then both blocks are stored with one mvout each; kb=0 uses overwrite mode to initialize, kb=1,2 accumulate, giving the exact K=48 ordered reduction. The A tiles for kb=0 (both m-blocks) persist in scratchpad rows 0-31 across all three n-block passes; B tiles stream into rows 32-47; the kb=1,2 A tiles stream into rows 48-63, where the A(m1) tile reuses the same 16 rows after the A(m0) tile was consumed by its compute. Each B tile is loaded once and reused for both m-blocks via a second preload of the same intact scratchpad rows, so B is loaded exactly 9 times and A 14 times: 23 mvins x 256 bytes = 5888 total DMA input bytes, the minimum for this schedule shape given the 64-row scratchpad, with 70 commands and a final fence.

proposal.rationale: Weight-stationary dataflow, n-blocks outer, k-blocks inner per m-block. All three A(m0,k) tiles persist in scratchpad rows 0-47 for the entire run; a single 16-row streaming slot (rows 48-63) alternates between the current B(k,n) tile and the current A(m1,k) tile. Each B(k,n) is loaded once, used by the (m0,n,k) compute (which latches it), and the (m1,n,k) compute then reuses the latched B via accumulated=true with a GARBAGE preload, so the A(m1,k) mvin may overwrite the B scratchpad copy. Per C tile the computes run k=0 (overwrite, initializing the accumulator) then k=1,2 (accumulate), giving the exact K=48 ordered reduction; both C tiles of the n-block are mvout once each after k=2. Total mvins: 3 persistent A(m0) + 9 streamed A(m1) + 9 B = 21 tiles x 256 bytes = 5376 DMA input bytes (a strict lower bound: 9 B tiles must each load once, and at most 3 of 6 A tiles can persist across n-blocks within the 64-row scratchpad), with 68 commands and a final fence.
